lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is a special meeting of the Telluride Medical Center board to consider formally engaging a consultant for due diligence with CommonSpirit Health — one of the country's largest hospital systems — which signals a potential affiliation or transaction that could reshape local healthcare for good. Meanwhile, Ouray City Council holds a public hearing on its 2027 budget and votes on two ordinances setting utility rates and adding a new light-industrial rate category, and Telluride's Ecology Commission takes up a draft ordinance that would ban gas-powered lawn equipment in town limits by 2028 and 2030.

notable.stake: Board votes on CommonSpirit due diligence — could reshape local healthcare permanently.
